id: lessons/7323-Why Anything to the Power of 0 Equals 1/lesson.json
title: Why Anything to the Power of 0 Equals 1

elements.content: Hold still. I'm making you twice your size.
What power should we set to make Pesto 4 times bigger?

2² = 2 x 2 = 4

I'll now make you
4 times bigger...
What power should we set to make Pesto 8 times bigger?
I want to go back to normal!
Don't worry! I'll set it to 0.

2⁰ will get you back
 to size 1.
Okay okay, put me back! Normal size! Please!
Relax. I'll just set it to zero.
Zero?! Two to the zero is zero! I'm about to disappear!
He thinks nonexistence is a setting on the dial.
Obviously. Zero zaps means untouched. Not gone.
Look at the pattern instead of panicking next time.
So dial at zero just means... my normal size. 1 times myself.
Anything divided by itself is 1. Even Pesto could get this one.
Dividing powers means subtracting exponents. 3 minus 3 is 0.
Works for any number. Big, small, negative.
Which one is NOT equal to 1?

options: Each step back undoes a doubling, and 2 ÷ 2 = 1
It's a rule with no reason

elements.content: Any nonzero number to the power 0 equals 1. Why: each step down divides by the base. 2³ = 8 → 2² = 4 → 2¹ = 2 → 2⁰ = 1 Also: aⁿ ÷ aⁿ = a⁰, and anything ÷ itself = 1. Not 0. Not the base. 1. *(0⁰ is a special case — skip it for now.)*
